correctness.rationale: For a fixed supercritical q the final susceptibility is on the lower branch below the peak q^(1/p); taking the seed to zero selects the nontrivial root of 1-s=q integral_s^1 u^(-p)du by strict concavity and continuity. Every interior s produces q in (0,1) with s<q^(1/p)<1, and the objective is positive inside and vanishes at the endpoints. For fixed s, h_p is the reciprocal L^p norm of the nonconstant 1/U_s, so evaluation at the larger exponent's interior maximizer gives strict decrease. At p=2 the objective is sqrt(s)-s, maximized at s=1/4. At large p, the bound on s<=1-epsilon loses a fixed fraction of log p; the band 1-s<=p^(-1/2) has at most (1/2+o(1))log p. On the intervening band, the exponent in h_p/s has size O(log p/p), so the uniform error in p(h_p-s) is O((log p)^2/p) plus an exponentially small term. The resulting strictly concave F_L has interior maximizer y=1/(1+z) with z+log z=L-1 and value z; it beats both edges. This proves the o(1) remainder and the claimed log-log correction. A separate 20,000-point grid with local refinement gave M(2)=0.25, M(2.5)=0.2323013, M(3)=0.2174250 and M(20)=0.0812554; this is finite corroboration only.
residual_risks: No bound uniform in the initial seed or pointwise exponent ordering at fixed q is asserted. Numerical samples do not certify the infinite-parameter statements.

value.rationale: The classical post-peak burden question motivates the same maximization for nonlinear incidence. Known individual values do not describe how that bound changes as the exponent varies. Strict decay and the sharp log-log correction resolve that family-level question rather than just supplying another numerical instance. This is an abstract-model result, not a forecast or claim about arbitrary epidemics.
residual_risks: No empirical estimate or extension to finite seeds, heterogeneous contact, or stochastic epidemics is established.
